title: Lunceford's Fisk origins and hits before Young joined
summary: The founding members came from Fisk; Lunceford was already successful when Young joined.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I understand -- I wasn't with him then, but I understand that some of the guys came right out of school with him, out of Fisk, you know. And the drummer, Jimmy Crawford, somebody told me that he taught Crawford in school in Memphis, and when Jimmy left school, he went to teaching, you know. But Jimmy Wilcox, Willie Smith, Earl Caruthers and some other guys was in the band before that I didn't meet -- Andrew Brown. They all went to Fisk University together.
Why, had they had the band in college or were they just friends in college?

I don't know. They could have had a band in college. It would -- I really didn't know them back there then, because when I went with Lunceford, he was already on top. He was organized, you know. He had made several hit records.

"For Dancers Only" he'd already made. He'd already made "My Blue Heaven," "Charmaine," quite a few nice records, recordings, he had going when I went with him. So I didn't know them when they really were struggling, you know, and they really had -- of course, we never made a lot of money -- but I mean when they really had lean days, hard, rough days, I didn't -- I didn't know them then at the time.
